mainTopic: Juice squeezed into food (משקה הבא לאוכל), liquid going to waste, and which kinds of squeezing are forbidden on שבת
overview: The גמרא asks whether juice squeezed from fruit straight into food counts as 'food' or as 'liquid' (משקה הבא לאוכל). This matters because only liquid can make food able to become impure. A ברייתא about an impure person squeezing grapes seems to show the juice is liquid, but the ברייתא is explained as squeezing into an empty bowl. רבי ירמיה links the question to a dispute between תנאים about smoothing bread with grapes. רב פפא instead says that dispute is about liquid that goes to waste, and he links it to a ברייתא about cutting olives. רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע then separates the two cases. Next, רב rules that on שבת one may squeeze grapes into a pot of food but not into a bowl, and fish for brine even into a bowl. רב דימי confirms to אביי that this ruling comes from רב, not שמואל. The גמרא then quotes the three-way dispute of רב, שמואל and רבי יוחנן about squeezing pickled and boiled vegetables, and shows how each of them reads a challenging ברייתא. It ends with רב's rule that by Torah law only treading olives and grapes makes one liable, and begins a teaching about hearsay testimony that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the ברייתא: exactly an egg-volume stays pure, more becomes impure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes quoting a ברייתא about an impure person who squeezes grapes or olives. Exactly a כביצה gives pure juice, and from this we infer that more than a כביצה gives impure juice.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he squeezed exactly an egg-volume, the juice is pure. This implies that if he squeezed more than an egg-volume, the juice is impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a quote from a ברייתא and drawing an inference from it. This sets up a challenge that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food smaller than a כביצה cannot become impure. Once the first drop leaves an exact כביצה of fruit, the fruit is smaller than a כביצה, so the juice stays pure. If the fruit was more than a כביצה, it can become impure and pass impurity to the juice. The גמרא reads this as showing that the juice is able to become impure.

keyTerms.meaning: the volume of an egg, the minimum size of food that can become impure
exact, precisely measured
ritually pure / ritually impure
'this implies', used to draw an inference from what was just said

phrases.english: Exactly an egg-volume: the juice is pure.
phrases.notes: This is the end of a ברייתא that began in the previous section.

phrases.english: This implies that more than an egg-volume makes the juice impure.
phrases.notes: An inference drawn from the ברייתא.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא יוֹתֵר מִכְּבֵיצָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the source quoted on the previous amud, which tests the question of משקה הבא לאוכל.
steps.raayaObject: That the squeezed juice can become impure.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about an impure person squeezing olives and grapes.

steps.title: If the juice counts as food, how was it ever made susceptible?
steps.stepSummary: If juice squeezed into food is itself 'food', then nothing liquid ever touched it to make it susceptible to impurity. So how could it become impure?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that liquid that comes into food is food, then how did it become susceptible to impurity?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the ברייתא to challenge the view that juice going into food counts as food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food can only become impure after it has been wetted by a liquid (הכשר). If the juice is classified as food, no liquid was ever involved, so it should never be able to become impure. Yet the ברייתא says it does become impure, which suggests the juice is treated as liquid.

keyTerms.meaning: liquid that comes out of one food and goes into another food
it became susceptible (to impurity), from הֶכְשֵׁר
'and if you say', which introduces the position being attacked

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up 'becoming impure' with 'becoming susceptible.' Food first needs הכשר through a liquid, and only then can it become טמא. The question here is about the הכשר step.

phrases.english: And if you say
that liquid that comes into food is food,
by what means was it made susceptible?
phrases.notes: A rhetorical question that works as a challenge.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ מַשְׁקֶה הַבָּא לְאוֹכֶל אוֹכֶל הוּא בְּמַאי אִיתַּכְשַׁר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the inference from step 1 to attack one side of the question.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that משקה הבא לאוכל אוכל הוא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Impurity requires הכשר by liquid. If the juice is food, nothing could have made it susceptible, but the ברייתא says it becomes impure.

steps.title: Answer: he squeezed into an empty bowl
steps.stepSummary: The same Sage who raised the challenge also answers it. The ברייתא is talking about squeezing into an empty bowl, not into food, so the juice is plain liquid.
steps.simpleTranslation: He himself raised the challenge and he himself answered it: the case is where he squeezed into a bowl.
steps.whatsHappening: The challenge is answered. The ברייתא was never about juice going into food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is moved to one where the juice lands in an empty bowl. In that case it is liquid according to everyone, so it can become impure. The ברייתא therefore proves nothing about juice that goes into food, so the גמרא looks for another source in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: raises an objection
resolves, answers the objection
bowl

phrases.aramaic: הוּא מוֹתֵיב לַהּ וְהוּא מְפָרֵק לַהּ:
phrases.english: He raised the objection and he resolved it:
phrases.notes: The same אמורא both challenged and answered.

phrases.english: It refers to one who squeezes into a bowl.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא מוֹתֵיב לַהּ וְהוּא מְפָרֵק לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא proves that juice going into food is liquid.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about squeezing into an empty bowl, so it says nothing about juice going into food.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא about the impure person squeezing grapes does not settle the question, because it is about squeezing into a bowl.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה: this question is a dispute between תנאים
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה says our question matches a dispute in a משנה. There, someone smooths bread with grapes: the תנא קמא says the bread is not made susceptible, and רבי יהודה says it is.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: this is like a dispute between תנאים. If someone smooths bread with grapes, it was not made susceptible. רבי יהודה says: it was made susceptible.
steps.whatsHappening: A new approach begins. רבי ירמיה brings a משנה with a dispute that he will soon link to our question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone squeezes grape juice onto dough to give it a smooth surface before baking. The juice goes straight from one food (the grapes) onto another food (the bread). The תנאים argue whether this juice makes the bread susceptible.

keyTerms.meaning: 'like the תנאים', meaning this question is already argued about by תנאים
one who smooths (the surface of bread or dough)
it was made susceptible to impurity

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said: it is like a dispute of tannaim.
One who smooths bread with grapes: it was not made susceptible.
phrases.notes: The view of the תנא קמא.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: it was made susceptible.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה כְּתַנָּאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the ברייתא failed to settle the question, a new source is brought.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Smoothing bread with grapes: the תנא קמא says it is not made susceptible, and רבי יהודה says it is.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה: they argue whether juice going into food counts as food
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה explains that the dispute is exactly our question. The תנא קמא holds the juice is food, so it cannot make the bread susceptible. רבי יהודה holds it is not food but liquid, so it does.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it not that they argue about this? One Sage holds that liquid coming into food is food, and the other holds it is not food.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה connects the משנה's dispute to our question about משקה הבא לאוכל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the grape juice is classified as food, the bread was never wetted by a liquid, so it is not made susceptible. That is the תנא קמא. If the juice is liquid, it makes the bread susceptible, which is רבי יהודה. On this reading, our question is simply this old argument between תנאים.

keyTerms.meaning: 'is it not that...?', which offers a suggested explanation
they disagree
one Sage holds

phrases.english: Is it not that they disagree about this:

phrases.aramaic: מָר סָבַר מַשְׁקֶה הַבָּא לְאוֹכֶל — אוֹכֶל הוּא,
phrases.english: one Sage holds that liquid that comes into food is food,
phrases.notes: The תנא קמא, who rules the bread is not made susceptible.

phrases.english: and the other Sage holds that it is not food.
phrases.notes: רבי יהודה, who rules the bread is made susceptible.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי לָאו בְּהָא קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the dispute quoted in step 4.
steps.raayaObject: That the question of משקה הבא לאוכל is a dispute between תנאים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about smoothing bread with grapes.

steps.title: רב פפא: everyone agrees it is not food; they argue about liquid going to waste
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא rejects רבי ירמיה's reading. Everyone agrees that juice going into food is not food. The real argument is about liquid that will be lost, such as juice that dries up in the oven's heat.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: everyone agrees that liquid coming into food is not food. Here they argue about liquid that goes to waste. One Sage holds it is liquid, and the other holds it is not liquid.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא pushes back on רבי ירמיה. He offers a different explanation of what the תנאים are arguing about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The juice smeared on the bread will dry up in the oven, so it is 'going to waste.' רבי יהודה holds that such liquid still counts as liquid and makes the bread susceptible. The תנא קמא holds it does not count as liquid. On this reading, the משנה tells us nothing about משקה הבא לאוכל.

keyTerms.meaning: everyone agrees
liquid that is going to waste and will be lost
'and here', meaning in this case

steps.confusionAlert: רב פפא is not saying the juice is food. He says everyone agrees it is not food. The argument has simply moved to a different issue.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:

phrases.aramaic: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא מַשְׁקֶה הַבָּא לְאוֹכֶל לָאו אוֹכֶל הוּא,
phrases.english: everyone agrees that liquid coming into food is not food,
and here they disagree about liquid that goes to waste:
phrases.notes: The juice dries up from the oven's heat.

phrases.english: one Sage holds it is liquid,
phrases.notes: רבי יהודה

phrases.english: and the other Sage holds it is not liquid.
phrases.notes: The תנא קמא

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי ירמיה's explanation of the dispute in step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the link between the bread dispute and the question of משקה הבא לאוכל.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The dispute can be explained by another factor: the liquid is going to waste.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the question of משקה הבא לאוכל is still not settled by the משנה, and it introduces a new idea: משקה הבא לאיבוד.

steps.title: רב פפא's dispute also appears in a ברייתא about cutting olives
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the same disagreement about liquid going to waste appears elsewhere. A ברייתא discusses cutting olives with impure hands, with three cases, and רבי יהודה disagrees in the last one.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this follows the dispute of these תנאים, as it was taught: one who cuts olives with impure hands, they are made susceptible. If he cut them to dip in salt, they are not made susceptible. If he cut them to check whether the olives are ready to harvest, they are not made susceptible. רבי יהודה says: they are made susceptible.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא supports his approach. He shows that a known dispute between תנאים is about exactly this idea of liquid going to waste.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are three cases. Cutting olives in general makes them susceptible. Cutting them to dip in salt does not, because the owner does not want the juice that comes out. Cutting to test ripeness is the disputed case: the juice is wasted, and רבי יהודה still says it makes the olives susceptible.

keyTerms.meaning: a dispute
one who cuts or cracks open (olives)
impure hands
to harvest olives

phrases.english: And this is the dispute of these tannaim, as it was taught:
One who cuts olives with impure hands: they were made susceptible.
To dip them in salt: they were not made susceptible.
phrases.notes: The juice came out against the owner's wishes.

phrases.aramaic: לֵידַע אִם הִגִּיעוּ זֵיתָיו לִמְסוֹק אִם לָאו — לֹא הוּכְשַׁר.
phrases.english: To know whether his olives are ready to harvest or not: they were not made susceptible.
phrases.notes: The disputed case.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: they were made susceptible.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבִפְלוּגְתָּא דְהָנֵי תַּנָּאֵי דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב פפא's approach by linking it to another dispute between תנאים.
steps.raayaObject: That the question of liquid going to waste is a known dispute between תנאים.

steps.title: The olive dispute is about liquid going to waste
steps.stepSummary: The olive dispute is explained the same way. רבי יהודה holds that liquid going to waste is still liquid, and the תנא קמא holds it is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it not that they argue about this? One Sage holds that liquid going to waste is liquid, and the other holds it is not liquid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the olive dispute as the same argument רב פפא described.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When olives are cut to test ripeness, the juice that comes out is simply lost. רבי יהודה says it still counts as liquid and makes the olives susceptible. The תנא קמא says it does not. This matches the bread case as רב פפא read it.

keyTerms.meaning: liquid that is set to be lost or wasted

steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to explain the bread-and-grapes dispute. רבי ירמיה says it is about משקה הבא לאוכל. רב פפא says it is about משקה הבא לאיבוד, the same argument as in the olive ברייתא. The next step challenges רב פפא's claim that the two disputes are the same.

phrases.english: Is it not that they disagree about this:

phrases.aramaic: דְּמָר סָבַר מַשְׁקֶה הָעוֹמֵד לְאִיבּוּד — מַשְׁקֶה הוּא,
phrases.english: that one Sage holds liquid set to go to waste is liquid,
phrases.notes: רבי יהודה

phrases.english: and the other Sage holds it is not liquid.
phrases.notes: The תנא קמא

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי לָאו בְּהָא קָמִיפַּלְגִי דְּמָר סָבַר מַשְׁקֶה הָעוֹמֵד לְאִיבּוּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the olive dispute quoted in step 7.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Whether liquid going to waste counts as liquid is a dispute between תנאים: רבי יהודה says yes, and the תנא קמא says no.

steps.title: The bread case and the olive case are different arguments
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע says the olive dispute is about liquid that will go to waste. The bread dispute is about liquid used to make the bread shine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא, son of רב יהושע, said: These תנאים (in the olive case) argue about liquid that is going to waste. Those תנאים (in the bread case) argue about liquid that is meant to make the bread shine.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע disagrees with רב פפא's claim that both disputes are the same argument. He gives each dispute its own topic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the olive case, the juice really is wasted, so the question there is whether wasted liquid still counts as a liquid. In the bread case, the grape juice is not wasted at all. It is used on purpose to give the bread a shine, so that dispute is about liquid used for polishing.

keyTerms.meaning: to make it shine or to polish it
these תנאים / those תנאים (the two different pairs of disputants)
they are arguing about

steps.whatToRemember: There are two separate questions here. The olive case asks about liquid going to waste. The bread case asks about liquid used to make bread shine.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua said:

phrases.aramaic: הָנֵי תַּנָּאֵי בְּמַשְׁקֶה הָעוֹמֵד לְאִיבּוּד פְּלִיגִי,
phrases.english: These tanna'im argue about liquid that stands to go to waste,
phrases.notes: This refers to the olive case.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָנָךְ תַּנָּאֵי בְּמַשְׁקֶה הָעוֹמֵד לְצַחְצְחוֹ קָמִיפַּלְגִי.
phrases.english: and those tanna'im argue about liquid that stands to make it shine.
phrases.notes: This refers to the bread smoothed with grapes.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי תַּנָּאֵי בְּמַשְׁקֶה הָעוֹמֵד לְאִיבּוּד פְּלִיגִי, וְהָנָךְ תַּנָּאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the idea from Steps 7-8 that the olive dispute and the bread dispute are the same argument.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the claim that the two disputes are the same is rejected. Each dispute still stands on its own.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The juice on the bread is not wasted. It is used on purpose for shine, so it is not the same as the wasted olive juice.

steps.title: Squeezing grapes into a pot but not a bowl, and fish for brine
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that on שבת a person may squeeze grapes into a pot of food but not into a bowl. A fish may be squeezed for its brine even into a bowl.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said in the name of רב חייא בר אשי, quoting רב: A person may squeeze a cluster of grapes into a pot, but not into a bowl. And a fish may be squeezed for its brine even into a bowl.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new practical rule about squeezing on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When juice goes straight into food in a pot, it is treated as part of the food, so this is not forbidden squeezing. Squeezing into an empty bowl produces a plain drink, which is forbidden. Fish brine is not treated as a real 'liquid' in this sense, so squeezing it is allowed even into a bowl.

keyTerms.meaning: squeezes (out liquid)
a cluster of grapes
a cooking pot, which has food in it
a bowl, which is empty or holds liquid
brine, the salty liquid from fish

steps.confusionAlert: The difference between the pot and the bowl is not about the dish itself. It is about where the juice ends up. Juice going into food counts as food. Juice going into an empty bowl counts as a drink.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said that Rav Chiya bar Ashi said that Rav said:

phrases.aramaic: סוֹחֵט אָדָם אֶשְׁכּוֹל שֶׁל עֲנָבִים לְתוֹךְ הַקְּדֵרָה,
phrases.english: A person may squeeze a cluster of grapes into a pot,
phrases.notes: The pot contains food, so the juice becomes part of the food.

phrases.english: but not into a bowl.
And a fish for its brine, even into a bowl.

steps.triggerLanguage: סוֹחֵט אָדָם אֶשְׁכּוֹל שֶׁל עֲנָבִים לְתוֹךְ הַקְּדֵרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new practical discussion about squeezing on שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: It is allowed to squeeze grapes into food in a pot, but not into a bowl. It is allowed to squeeze fish for brine even into a bowl.

steps.title: אביי says the rule is hard if it comes from שמואל
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי teaches the rule. אביי says that in רב's name it causes no problem, but his group teaches it in שמואל's name. He asks: did שמואל really allow squeezing a fish into a bowl?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב דימי sat and taught this rule. אביי said to רב דימי: You teach it in the name of רב, so it is not hard for you. We teach it in the name of שמואל, so it is hard for us: Did שמואל really say a fish may be squeezed for its brine even into a bowl?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי raises a challenge against the fish part of the rule, if the rule comes from שמואל. This step sets up the next step, which brings the source that causes the problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule itself is not attacked. The attack is on who said it. If שמואל said it, it seems to contradict something else שמואל said, and the גמרא is about to quote that statement.

keyTerms.meaning: a teaching or rule
you teach / we teach
in the name of
it is difficult for us

phrases.aramaic: יָתֵיב רַב דִּימִי וְקָאָמַר לַהּ לְהָא שְׁמַעְתָּא.
phrases.english: Rav Dimi sat and was saying this teaching.
Abaye said to Rav Dimi:

phrases.aramaic: אַתּוּן מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב מַתְנִיתוּן וְלָא קַשְׁיָא לְכוּ,
phrases.english: You teach it in the name of Rav, and it is not difficult for you;

phrases.aramaic: אֲנַן מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל מַתְנִינַן לַהּ, וְקַשְׁיָא לַן:
phrases.english: we teach it in the name of Shmuel, and it is difficult for us:
Did Shmuel really say a fish for its brine
even into a bowl?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתּוּן מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב מַתְנִיתוּן וְלָא קַשְׁיָא לְכוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the fish part of Step 10 if שמואל is the one who said it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a fish may be squeezed for brine even into a bowl, when it is said in שמואל's name.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל seems to forbid squeezing food for its liquid. This rule allows exactly that with fish. So he would be contradicting himself.

steps.title: רב and שמואל on squeezing pickled and boiled vegetables
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the source behind אביי's question. רב treats pickled and boiled vegetables differently. שמואל treats both the same: squeezing them for their liquid is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was stated: Pickled vegetables that someone squeezed. רב said: If he squeezed them for the vegetables themselves, it is permitted. If he squeezed them for their liquid, he is exempt, but it is forbidden. Boiled vegetables, whether for themselves or for their liquid, are permitted. שמואל said: Both pickled and boiled vegetables are the same. For themselves, it is permitted. For their liquid, he is exempt, but it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source that proves אביי's challenge. In this source, שמואל forbids squeezing even boiled vegetables for their liquid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Squeezing a fish for its brine is like squeezing boiled vegetables for their liquid. רב allows squeezing boiled vegetables for their liquid, so his fish rule fits his view. שמואל forbids it, so a fish rule allowing this in his name looks like a contradiction.

steps.title: רב דימי swears his tradition comes from רב
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי answers אביי with an oath that he heard the teaching in רב's name. He lists the chain of teachers: רבי ירמיה, רבי זירא, רב חייא בר אשי, and רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: By God! "My eyes have seen, and not a stranger's." I heard it from the mouth of רבי ירמיה. רבי ירמיה heard it from רבי זירא, רבי זירא heard it from רב חייא בר אשי, and רב חייא בר אשי heard it from רב.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי answers אביי's question by insisting that the teaching about squeezing a fish belongs to רב. He says he heard it with his own ears, through a reliable chain of teachers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי had no problem if the teaching was in רב's name. His problem was only with the version that said it came from שמואל, because שמואל elsewhere forbids squeezing for liquid. By confirming that the teaching comes from רב, רב דימי makes the contradiction with שמואל disappear.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting the attribution: the teaching belongs to רב, not שמואל
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The teaching about squeezing a fish was שמואל's, which would contradict שמואל's own view.
steps.terutzMaskana: The teaching is רב's, as passed down through a reliable chain, so there is no contradiction.

steps.title: רב's full ruling on pickled and boiled vegetables
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now quotes the full dispute it referred to earlier. רב says squeezing כבשים for the vegetable itself is allowed, and squeezing them for their liquid is פטור אבל אסור. Squeezing שלקות is allowed either way.
steps.simpleTranslation: The matter itself: Pickled vegetables that a person squeezed. רב said: If he squeezed them for the vegetables themselves, it is permitted. If he squeezed them for their liquid, he is פטור but it is אסור. Boiled vegetables, whether squeezed for themselves or for their liquid, are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The word גופא tells us the גמרא is going back to quote the earlier source in full, so it can study it properly. It starts with רב's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב treats pickled vegetables as having real liquid. So squeezing them to get that liquid is rabbinically forbidden, though there is no חטאת. Boiled vegetables are different: the water they absorbed does not count as their own liquid, so squeezing them is fully allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: "The matter itself": going back to quote and examine a source mentioned earlier
Pickled vegetables
Boiled vegetables
For the vegetables themselves (to remove extra liquid so they can be eaten)
For their liquid (to collect and use the juice)
No חטאת is brought, but it is still forbidden (a rabbinic prohibition)

steps.confusionAlert: פטור here does NOT mean "allowed." It only means there is no Torah-level liability. The action is still אסור.

phrases.english: The matter itself.
Pickled vegetables that one squeezed, Rav said:
for themselves — it is permitted,
for their liquid — he is exempt, but it is forbidden.

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁלָקוֹת, בֵּין לְגוּפָן בֵּין לְמֵימֵיהֶן — מוּתָּר.
phrases.english: And boiled vegetables, whether for themselves or for their liquid — it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא. כְּבָשִׁים שֶׁסְּחָטָן, אָמַר רַב

steps.title: שמואל treats pickled and boiled vegetables the same
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says that both pickled and boiled vegetables follow the same rule. Squeezing them for themselves is allowed, and squeezing them for their liquid is פטור אבל אסור.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: Both this and that: for themselves, it is permitted; for their liquid, he is פטור but it is אסור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives שמואל's opinion, which disagrees with רב about boiled vegetables.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב and שמואל agree about pickled vegetables. They argue only about boiled vegetables. שמואל holds that the liquid squeezed from boiled vegetables also counts, so squeezing it out is rabbinically forbidden, just like with pickled vegetables.

keyTerms.meaning: שמואל, an early אמורא of Bavel who often disputes with רב
Both this and that: here, pickled and boiled vegetables alike
Permitted

phrases.english: And Shmuel said: both this and that,
for themselves — it is permitted,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second opinion that disagrees with רב about boiled vegetables.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Pickled and boiled vegetables alike: for themselves, permitted; for their liquid, פטור אבל אסור.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: squeezing for liquid brings a sin-offering
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says that for both pickled and boiled vegetables, squeezing them for themselves is allowed. But squeezing them for their liquid makes a person חייב חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Both pickled vegetables and boiled vegetables: for themselves, it is permitted; for their liquid, he is חייב חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the third and strictest opinion, that of רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן treats the liquid of both kinds of vegetables as real liquid at the Torah level. So squeezing it out is a full מלאכה, and a person who does it by accident must bring a חטאת. All three opinions agree that squeezing for the vegetable itself is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: רבי יוחנן, a leading אמורא of ארץ ישראל
Must bring a sin-offering: he did a Torah-level מלאכה by accident
Both pickled and boiled vegetables

steps.whatToRemember: Three views on squeezing vegetables for their liquid. רב: pickled is אסור, boiled is מותר. שמואל: both are אסור (rabbinic). רבי יוחנן: both make a person חייב חטאת. All agree that squeezing for the vegetable itself is allowed.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אֶחָד כְּבָשִׁים וְאֶחָד שְׁלָקוֹת,

steps.title: A ברייתא seems to challenge all three opinions
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a person may squeeze pickled vegetables on שבת for use on שבת, without any limit. That seems to allow squeezing even for the liquid, which goes against רב, שמואל, and רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from a ברייתא: One may squeeze pickled vegetables on שבת for the needs of שבת, but not for after שבת. And olives and grapes one may not squeeze, and if he did squeeze them, he is חייב חטאת. This is difficult for רב, difficult for שמואל, and difficult for רבי יוחנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to allow squeezing pickled vegetables in every case. That clashes with all three opinions just quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא allows squeezing pickled vegetables and does not separate squeezing for the vegetable from squeezing for the liquid. All three אמוראים forbid squeezing pickled vegetables for their liquid in some way. So the plain reading of the ברייתא challenges every one of them.

keyTerms.meaning: They challenged: a challenge from a תנאי source
One may squeeze
For the needs of שבת (to use on שבת itself)
After שבת ends
Olives and grapes: fruits squeezed mainly for their liquid

steps.title: Each אמורא explains the ברייתא his own way

steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of rejecting any opinion, the גמרא says the ברייתא is short and leaves things out. Each אמורא will fill in the missing details to match his own ruling.

steps.title: How רב reads the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רב adds words to the ברייתא. The permission to squeeze pickled vegetables is only for the vegetables themselves. For their liquid it is פטור אבל אסור. Boiled vegetables are allowed either way, and olives and grapes bring a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב explains it according to his reasoning: One may squeeze pickled vegetables on שבת for the needs of שבת, but not for after שבת. When was this said? When squeezing them for themselves. But for their liquid, he is פטור but it is אסור. Boiled vegetables, whether for themselves or for their liquid, are permitted. And olives and grapes one may not squeeze, and if he squeezed them, he is חייב חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how רב reads the ברייתא, adding words so that it matches his ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words במה דברים אמורים limit the ברייתא's permission to squeezing the vegetables for themselves. Squeezing pickled vegetables for their liquid becomes פטור אבל אסור, and boiled vegetables are allowed. These are exactly רב's rulings from step 14, so the challenge to him is answered.

steps.title: שמואל reads the ברייתא to fit his view
steps.stepSummary: שמואל adds words to the ברייתא. Pickled and boiled vegetables follow the same rule. Squeezing them for themselves is allowed. Squeezing them for their liquid is פטור אבל אסור. Olives and grapes bring a חטאת.

steps.deeperAnalysis: רב had treated boiled vegetables as different from pickled ones. שמואל puts them together under one rule. For both kinds, squeezing for the vegetable itself is allowed, and squeezing for the liquid is פטור אבל אסור. Olives and grapes stay in a separate, stricter group that brings a חטאת.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן reads the ברייתא to fit his view
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן adds words to the ברייתא. You may squeeze pickled and boiled vegetables for שבת, but not for after שבת, and only for the vegetables themselves. Squeezing for the liquid counts like squeezing olives and grapes, so the person is חייב חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן explains the ברייתא his own way: You may squeeze pickled vegetables for use on שבת, but not for after שבת. This is true for both pickled and boiled vegetables. steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן puts pickled and boiled vegetables under one rule. Squeezing them for the vegetables themselves is allowed on שבת for שבת use. He is the strictest of the three about the liquid: squeezing vegetables for their liquid is treated exactly like squeezing olives and grapes, which brings a full חטאת.

but for their liquid, one may not squeeze,

steps.title: By Torah law, a person is חייב only for treading olives and grapes
steps.stepSummary: רב חייא בר אשי quotes רב: by Torah law, a person is חייב only for treading olives and grapes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חייא בר אשי said in the name of רב: By Torah law, a person is liable only for treading olives and grapes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new statement from רב that sets the Torah-level limit of this מלאכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah-level חיוב of squeezing applies only to olives and grapes, the fruits that are normally pressed for their juice. This fits רב's own view in Step 19, where only olives and grapes bring a חטאת. Every other kind of squeezing is forbidden only by the חכמים.

keyTerms.meaning: By Torah law (not a rabbinic rule)
Treading or pressing down to get juice out
Only (literally: "it is not... except")

steps.whyThisMatters: It draws the line between Torah-level squeezing (olives and grapes) and squeezing that the חכמים forbade. That line explains why the other cases are only פטור אבל אסור in רב's view.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Chiyya bar Ashi said that Rav said:
By Torah law —
one is liable only for treading
olives and grapes alone.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the three readings of the ברייתא, the גמרא gives a general rule about which squeezing is forbidden by the Torah.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only treading olives and grapes is forbidden by the Torah. All other squeezing is forbidden by the חכמים.

steps.title: A ברייתא from the school of מנשה says the same
steps.stepSummary: The school of מנשה taught the same rule as רב: by Torah law, a person is חייב only for treading olives and grapes.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so it was taught in the school of מנשה: By Torah law, a person is liable only for treading olives and grapes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports רב's rule by showing that a ברייתא from the school of מנשה teaches the very same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word וְכֵן ("and so") tells us that a ברייתא agrees with the אמורא. This makes רב's rule stronger, because a תנאי source says the same words.

keyTerms.meaning: And so it was taught (introduces a supporting ברייתא)
The school (בית מדרש) of מנשה

phrases.english: And so it was taught in the school of Menashe:
By Torah law one is liable

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא עַל דְּרִיסַת זֵיתִים וַעֲנָבִים בִּלְבַד.
phrases.english: only for treading olives and grapes alone.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן תָּנֵי דְּבֵי מְנַשֶּׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב's statement in Step 22 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רב's rule that the Torah-level חיוב covers only olives and grapes
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא of the school of מנשה with the same wording

steps.title: A new teaching from the school of מנשה about a hearsay witness
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts listing another teaching of the school of מנשה, about a witness who testifies based on what he heard from another witness. This teaching continues in the next lines.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a witness who speaks from the mouth of another witness (hearsay testimony) is not valid (the sentence continues on the next amud: except in a specific case).
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא moves on to another teaching from the same school of מנשה, on a new subject: עד מפי עד. This line begins a list that continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This teaching has nothing to do with squeezing. It comes up only because it was taught in the same school. The גמרא often lists a few teachings of one source together.

keyTerms.meaning: A witness repeating what he heard from another witness (hearsay)
Valid

steps.confusionAlert: This line is a new topic, not part of the squeezing rules. The words "ואין... כשר" open an "אין... אלא" ("not... except") sentence that finishes on the next amud: hearsay testimony is not valid except in a specific case. That is why the Sefaria translation, which anticipates the ending, says "is valid." The two are not in conflict.

phrases.english: And a witness from the mouth of a witness is not valid
phrases.notes: This is the start of a "not valid except..." sentence. It is completed on the next amud, which is why Sefaria translates it as "is valid [only in a certain case]."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין עֵד מִפִּי עֵד כָּשֵׁר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It continues quoting the school of מנשה, but on a different subject.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A teaching about whether hearsay testimony (עד מפי עד) is valid. It is completed in the following text.
